Q: How to create a note with a checklist in Notes on macOS from script A:

In NoteStore.sqlite a note isn't HTML at all. It's a gzipped protobuf where checkbox state lives in AttributeRun.ParagraphStyle as style_type = 103 plus a Checklist { uuid, done } submessage. The body property AppleScript gives you is a rendering of that protobuf into HTML, and that rendering has no checkbox syntax. Notes has an HTML representation for dash lists and none for checklists.

So the only two routes are UI keystrokes spelled out by https://stackoverflow.com/a/79581471/12875823 or writing protobuf into NoteStore directly, which needs Full Disk Access and risks corrupting your live Notes database.

Q: How to download video of mp2t format from browser A:

Here's how I manage successfully to do it:

You will need win7 or later, FireFox, MKVTOOLNIX, TotalCommander, and a rename DateTimeMs tool I did in batch/powershell: https://sourceforge.net/p/rendatetime-batch/

Firefox must have higher cache size than the total streamed movie, usually 8Gb is enough, change FireFox settings in about:config

    browser.cache.disk.capacity = 8388608 [unit is KB]
    browser.cache.disk.parent_directory = C:\CACHE [I use ram disk in: B:\CACHE]

Get mkvtoolnix (for win7 here): https://forum.videohelp.com/threads/405407-NON-OFFICIAL-Windows-builds-of-MKVtoolnix/page15#post2799844

Get TotalCommander from Ghisler site

In FireFox go to movie site, just before playing the movie.

Manually delete CACHE, all files under (doesn't matter if can't delete all): C:\CACHE\cache2\entries

Start watching the movie, press pause immediatly, set highest resolution, speed up to 1.75x (had Audio synch issues at 2x).

Wait to finish, don't use other tabs in firefox.

Copy whole cache to a working place ie: COPY C:\CACHE\cache2\entries\*.* D:\SCRATCH

Go to SCRATCH dir, change extension to all extensionless files: ren *. *.mp2t

Using total commander sort by Size, mark (right click and drag) and delete all <15 Kbytes files

Rename all mp2t files to it's datetime using: renDateTime.bat *.mp2t

Sort by name, test playing first files, in my case all *.mp2t starts with "G@ ..." in totalCommander use F3 to view content of suspicious files.

Be sure to view first 5 files to check no repetitions of the begining at different resolutions, delete any incorrect file.

Open mkvToolNix-GUI, drag first MP2T file to it.

Select all the rest of the MP2T (EXCLUDING first file) and drag the hundreds files to MKVToolnix-GUI, when asked select 4th option "Add as additional parts...", OK.

You may change Destination name to MovieName, and START multiplexing.

Check different parts of the movie, specially the start and the end, watch for audio synch. MkvToolnix have ways to delay audio if needed. But use 1x if synch issues.

Q: Logic behind sizeof() for 2D arrays in C A:

In C, the sizeof operator is used to determine the size of an object in bytes.

In your case, to find the number of elements in the array, you take the size of the entire array and divide it by the size of a single element:

int size = sizeof(fruits) / sizeof(fruits[0]);

Since all elements of an array have the same size, dividing the total size of the array by the size of one element gives you the number of elements in the array.

You can think of it like a cake that has been cut into equal-sized slices. If the whole cake weighs 800 grams and each slice weighs 100 grams, then:

800 / 100 = 8 slices

Similarly, if the entire array occupies 30 bytes and each element occupies 10 bytes, then:

30 / 10 = 3 elements

So sizeof(fruits) / sizeof(fruits[0]) gives you the number of elements (rows) in the array.

Q: Can a Milvus BM25 function use a VARCHAR field added after data was sealed? A:

I would define the VARCHAR field and BM25 function before inserting data.

If the collection already contains sealed data and the text field was added later, the safer option is to create a new collection with the final schema and BM25 function, then migrate or reinsert the existing data.

So prefer:

define fields + BM25 function → create collection → insert data

instead of:

insert data → add VARCHAR field → add BM25 function

Q: Running MySQL get results and exit A:

You could run a mysql and specify a statement in command-line arguments that does nothing and has no result set.

For example:

mysql -e "do 1"

The DO statement is supported by MySQL but it doesn't get much air play.
See DO Statement documentation.

Q: Listener for property value changes in a Javascript object A:

As far as i can read, no answer relates to the OP's question:

Can someone please throw some good use cases where these functions will come in handy?

My use case: Imagine an object in an existing library that receives an options-object on instantiation, which is also available after it was created. Some of these config values can be altered during lifetime of that object, and on calling specific methods the next time, those will use these new config values.

However, now i have found an option that only has an effect if supplied during instantiation, i.e. b/c it will register certain event listeners – changing it afterwards updates the value but doesn't change the behavior. But i really need to turn this behavior on or off during runtime. Lets call that option doSomethingOnKeyDown for the sake of the argument.

How can i add a pull request to that library that doesn't fundamentally change the API?

I build a proxy:

  // … we're somewhere in the constructor
  this.options = new Proxy(this.options, {
    set: function (target, key, value) {
      if (key == 'doSomethingOnKeyDown' && value !== target[key]) {
        value === true 
          ? window.addEventListener('keydown', keydownHandler) 
          : window.removeEventListener('keydown', keydownHandler) 
      }
      
      target[key] = value // default behavior: store the value
      
      return true // Indicate success
    }
  })

Et voilá: now anyone can change this option on the object during runtime, i.e. myInstance.options.doSomethingOnKeyDown = false and it will update its behavior accordingly – and the API of the object stays the same.

Q: How to correctly apply causal masking in Keras Multi-Head Attention for multi-step time series forecasting? A:

MultiHeadAttention already has causal masking built in, so there is no need to create the triangular mask manually:

def call(self, inputs, training=False):
    attn_output = self.att(
        query=inputs,
        value=inputs,
        key=inputs,
        use_causal_mask=True,
        training=training,
    )

    attn_output = self.dropout1(attn_output, training=training)
    out1 = self.layernorm1(inputs + attn_output)

    ffn_output = self.ffn(out1)
    ffn_output = self.dropout2(ffn_output, training=training)

    return self.layernorm2(out1 + ffn_output)

This also works with a dynamic sequence length.

If you do build the mask yourself, (sequence_length, sequence_length) is sufficient. Keras broadcasts it across the batch and attention heads:

sequence_length = tf.shape(inputs)[1]

mask = tf.linalg.band_part(
    tf.ones(
        (sequence_length, sequence_length),
        dtype=tf.bool,
    ),
    -1,
    0,
)

attn_output = self.att(
    query=inputs,
    value=inputs,
    key=inputs,
    attention_mask=mask,
    training=training,
)

Looking at the model description, though, the encoder may not need this mask. If inputs contains only historical values available at the forecast origin, allowing those positions to attend to each other does not introduce target leakage.

The causal mask matters when previous target values are fed into an autoregressive decoder, or when the prediction at position t must not see positions after t.

Also check how the training windows are constructed. A causal mask will not prevent leakage if future target or climate values are already included in inputs.

See the MultiHeadAttention documentation for the accepted mask shapes and use_causal_mask.
